pages.title: SLAS Best Practices | SCAPI | B2C Commerce API | Salesforce Developers
pages.text:
# SLAS Best Practices

Follow best practices for the Shopper Login and API Access Service (SLAS) to maximize security and performance. Recommended steps include using a private client in production, using Strict Client Auth for private clients, offering passwordless login when your storefront supports it, and rotating a guest shopper’s session after they place an order.

Use a private SLAS client in production. A private client stores the client secret on your server, which keeps production authentication more secure than a public client. Use a private client for a full-stack web app or any app with a backend-for-frontend (BFF).

If you use PWA Kit or Storefront Next with Hybrid Auth, a private client is highly recommended for maximum security.

A public client is appropriate only when the app cannot store a client secret securely. The recommendation is to use a private client with a backend-for-frontend (BFF) layer.

For setup and login flows, see Private SLAS Client Use Cases.

Strict Client Auth is a highly recommended setting for private clients, which requires all `/login` and `/authorize` requests to pass their credentials directly in the `x-slas-client-auth` header. This feature is part of a broader set of protections to help keep authentication endpoints secure and resilient against automated threats. Public clients don’t support Strict Client Auth and ignore the `x-slas-client-auth` header if present.

Before you turn on Strict Client Auth for a client that a PWA Kit or Storefront Next storefront uses, upgrade the storefront to a version that sends the `x-slas-client-auth` header:

* Storefront Next 1.5.0 or later.
* PWA Kit 3.22.0 or later, using the SLAS private client proxy. If your PWA Kit storefront passes the client secret to `commerce-sdk-react` directly instead of using the proxy, social login (`/authorize`) doesn’t send the header.

Earlier storefront versions don’t send the header. If you turn on Strict Client Auth for a client that uses one of those versions, its `/login` and `/authorize` requests return a 401 Unauthorized error. Strict Client Auth still applies when your own backend sends the header.

Follow these steps to use Strict Client Auth.

1. From the SLAS Admin UI, create a new private client or edit an existing one.
2. Turn on **Strict Client Auth**. To review how Strict Client Auth interacts with the `x-slas-client-auth` header, expand the **Strict Client Auth Behavior Matrix** dropdown.

3. Save the private client.
4. Include a valid `x-slas-client-auth` header on requests to `/login` and `/authorize` endpoints. Requests that don’t include the header or include an invalid header return a 401 Unauthorized error. The header value must be a Base64-encoded string in the format `client_id:client_secret`.

SLAS validates the header against these criteria.

* The header value must be valid Base64.
* The decoded value must follow `client_id:client_secret` format with both values present.
* The `client_id` in the header must match the `client_id` query parameter.
* The `client_secret` must match the provisioned secret for the client.

SLAS validates the `x-slas-client-auth` header whenever it’s included in the request, regardless of whether the client has Strict Client Auth turned on.



Prefer passwordless login for shopper authentication when your storefront supports it. Passwordless login verifies a shopper’s identity without a password and offers protection against cyberattacks such as phishing and brute-force password cracking. SLAS supports one-time passwords (OTPs) and passkeys. For current storefront support, see Passwordless Login Feature Support.

As a best practice and to maximize security, send both `login_id` and `channel_id` on `POST /oauth2/passwordless/token` when you exchange a passwordless one-time password for an access token. Set `login_id` to the same value as the login identifier sent when the one-time password was requested (`user_id` on `POST /oauth2/passwordless/login`, or `login_id` when registering a customer). Don’t change spelling or capitalization. Set `channel_id` to the same site sent when the one-time password was requested. PWA Kit 3.22.0 or later and Storefront Next 1.5.0 or later send both values. If you upgraded only some storefront packages or customized the passwordless login pages, see Troubleshoot Passwordless Login for PWA Kit or Troubleshoot Passwordless Login for Storefront Next.

For a request example, see Exchange the TOTP for an Access Token.

Leaked Credentials Detection applies to `POST /shopper/auth/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/oauth2/login` because SLAS submits shopper credentials as HTTP Basic in the `Authorization` header. For a leaked-credentials match, use a SCAPI-zone rate-limiting rule with the `block` action (HTTP 429). Start the rule with the `log` action, review the matches, and then switch to `block`. Don’t use a `managed_challenge`, `js_challenge`, or `legacy_captcha` action. For storefront form login and rule examples, see Bot Management. For leaked-credentials detection and SCAPI-zone availability controls, see Security.

For an early warning of credential stuffing, turn on alerts for the login anomaly detector that Salesforce creates in Log Center. The detector doesn’t block login attempts. See Manage Anomaly Detectors in Log Center.

To protect against refresh-token replay abuse, SLAS limits how frequently a single refresh token can be exchanged at `/oauth2/token`.

* A refresh token can be exchanged up to 3 times within 60 seconds.
* Additional attempts return an HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) response with a `Retry-After` header.
* Repeated use of a revoked, expired, or unknown token can also return an HTTP 429 response.

To avoid hitting these limits, review your integration to make sure it doesn’t reuse or concurrently exchange the same refresh token, and make sure your application correctly handles HTTP 429 responses.

The SLAS Admin Delete Shopper endpoint is rate limited to 100 requests per minute per tenant by default.

* Requests that exceed this limit return an HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) response.
* When you receive a 429 response, wait before retrying. A 429 response blocks further requests until a 10-minute time-to-live (TTL) period expires. Requests sent before the TTL expires don’t return a valid response, so wait for the TTL to expire before retrying.

The SLAS limits in Refresh Token Service Protection and Delete Shopper Rate Limiting stay in place. A refresh token can be exchanged up to 3 times in 60 seconds, and Delete Shopper is limited to 100 requests per minute per tenant. Add rate-limiting rules on the SCAPI zone in Production Business Manager, in front of those limits. A rule applies to Development, Staging, and Production unless you scope it by the org ID in the URL path. See SCAPI Zone.

SLAS forwards `c_*` custom headers to ECOM on the `/login` endpoint. Use this to pass per-request context to third-party security and bot mitigation solutions integrated with your storefront.

To take advantage of this, prefix any custom header you want forwarded with `c_`.

The OAuth `state` parameter is preserved end-to-end through the Trusted Agent On Behalf (TAOB) flow, providing consistent state handling across the authorization and token requests. For details on passing the `state` parameter in a TAOB flow, see Specify TAOB Parameters for Guest Shoppers.

As a best practice, don’t validate or hardcode the specific value of the `aud` claim in your applications, as its format may change over time. Applications should rely on standard OAuth/OIDC token validation and use the `aud` claim only to verify that the token is intended for the receiving service, rather than matching a specific expected value.

Prevent guest order data from appearing in a shopper’s registered account by rotating the guest session immediately after receiving a guest order. Treat every completed guest order as a session boundary. In the recommended flow, after order confirmation, request a fresh guest token from SLAS using `grant_type=client_credentials`. Then, replace the currently stored access token and refresh token with the new ones.

If a guest later registers on the same device, the registered profile has no association with prior guest orders. By isolating guest sessions, you enable privacy-first guest shopping on retail kiosks, public computers, and shared devices where multiple guest shoppers browse and checkout sequentially.

The recommended flow triggers upon order confirmation, when a POST `/orders` request succeeds (1).

Ideally, make order confirmation the trigger for session rotation. This step marks the strongest boundary for guest shopper activity.  
Alternatively, use these trigger points, in order of preference:

1. After payment completion, if using a multi-step checkout with deferred order creation.
2. On logout. SLAS already handles this via `/logout`. However, this trigger doesn’t help if the guest never explicitly logs out befor

# Commerce Cloud

Develop personalized ecommerce experiences with our fast, flexible solutions.

## What's Commerce Cloud?

Salesforce Commerce Cloud offers distinct solutions for B2B/D2C (business-to-business and direct-to-consumer) and B2C (business-to-consumer) commerce. B2B and D2C Commerce solutions focus on complex order and account management, advanced personalization, and enterprise integration. B2C Commerce emphasizes high-volume transactions, customer engagement, seamless mobile-optimized checkout, and real-time inventory management. Not sure which product you have? See Which Salesforce Commerce Product Do I Have?

## Discover B2C Commerce

Get an introduction to our business-to-consumer (B2C) resources to build secure, scalable, and captivating ecommerce sites that convert shoppers. Not sure which product you have? See Which Salesforce Commerce Product Do I Have?

### B2C Commerce Overview

Learn how B2C Commerce can help you connect to shoppers, maximize revenue, and drive efficiency.

### Storefront Comparison

Understand the key differences between the various B2C options and which APIs and tools you can use with each option.

### Quick Start

Try out some basic steps for using storefront options such as Composable Storefront and Storefront Reference Architecture (SFRA).

### Developer Community

Join a vibrant global community of developers to ask questions, collaborate, and learn more about B2C Commerce.

## Build Your B2C Commerce Site

Implement a B2C Commerce storefront option. Create a headless site, use Storefront Next, or build a hybrid storefront.

### Get Started with B2C Commerce

Understand the recommended developer workflow to efficiently create a performant site on the B2C Commerce platform.

### B2C Commerce Architecture

Get a technical overview of the key concepts, initial setup, and essential tools to build and manage your storefront.

### Merchandise Your Site

Learn how to use Business Manager to set up your B2C Commerce data such as product and marketing information.

### Agentforce Commerce Vibes

Agentforce Commerce Vibes is a Visual Studio Code extension that helps you build, administer, and debug B2C storefront projects with AI-assisted chat and agent skills based on the Agentic B2C Developer Toolkit.

### Storefront Next

Create Storefront Next with modern web technologies, such as React 19 and Tailwind CSS, and host it on Managed Runtime. Get up and running with automated setup in Business Manager.

### Composable Storefront

Create a headless site with a fast and flexible architecture based on the Progressive Web App Kit and Managed Runtime.

### Storefront Reference Architecture (SFRA)

Build state-of-the-art shopping experiences faster with a mobile-optimized user experience and efficient, modern site architecture.

### Hybrid Storefront

To gradually migrate your site from SFRA to Composable Storefront, use a hybrid implementation.

### B2C Commerce on AppExchange

Find apps and certified consulting organizations to extend your B2C Commerce site and accelerate development.

### B2C Commerce Release Notes

Learn about new features and updates for B2C Commerce, API, SFRA Storefront, Composable Storefront, and Storefront Next.

## Customize and Extend Your B2C Commerce Site

Build your own custom B2C site or customize your headless, SFRA, or hybrid site with these APIs. Use these SDKs and our CLI to speed up development.

### B2C Commerce API (SCAPI)

Use a headless API to build custom apps. B2C Commerce API is also known as Salesforce Commerce API (SCAPI). Applies to: Composable, hybrid, and custom.

### Script API (B2C Commerce Developer Resources)

Customize ecommerce experiences using reference applications, Javascript-based APIs, and more. Applies to: Composable, SFRA, hybrid, and custom.

### Open Commerce API (OCAPI)

Access B2C Commerce data (such as product and shopper data) and functionality (such as baskets and orders) through secure and well-defined API methods. Applies to: Composable, SFRA, hybrid, and custom.

### Commerce SDK

Build Node.js applications that connect with B2C Commerce services using the Commerce SDK. Applies to: Composable, hybrid, and custom.

### Commerce SDK React

Use this collection of React Query hooks to fetch, cache, and mutate data from B2C Commerce API. Applies to: Composable, hybrid, and custom.

### Isomorphic Commerce SDK

Connects with B2C Commerce services from a Node.js app and web browser. Applies to: Composable, hybrid, and custom.

### Commerce Cloud CLI

Manage deployments and continuous integration using a CLI for B2C Commerce. Applies to: Composable, SFRA, hybrid, and custom.

### B2C Postman Collections

Work with B2C Commerce APIs using pre-built collections.

## Personalize Your B2C Commerce Site

Use Commerce Cloud Einstein to power up your B2C Commerce site with artificial intelligence (AI).

### Einstein Demo

Learn how Commerce Cloud Einstein can power personalized shopping experiences across shopper touchpoints.

### Deploy Einstein

Add AI-powered search, product recommendations, and shopper insights to your B2C Commerce site.

### Einstein API

Use B2C Commerce Einstein API to get personalized product recommendations.

### Einstein Guides

Learn how to use AI-powered merchandising tools to deliver actionable insights and tailored shopper experiences.

## Discover B2B and D2C Commerce

Explore this business-to-business (B2B) and direct-to-consumer (D2C) content to build secure, scalable sites. B2B sites are for shoppers such as retailers, wholesalers, or distributors who often make large purchases. Use our D2C option to sell products to the general public at a smaller scale than with B2C.

### Do I Have B2C, B2B, or D2C?

Find out which product you’re using so that you can access the correct documentation and resources.

### B2B and D2C Commerce

Design a B2B or D2C Commerce solution that uses the power of Lightning Experience to meet your business needs.

### Salesforce Commerce Extensions

Extensions enable fine-grained customization of B2B and D2C storefront functionality to meet your unique business needs and improve the shopper experience.

### Salesforce Order Management

Customize and integrate Salesforce Order Management with your ecommerce storefront, inventory, and fulfillment systems.

### B2B and D2C Postman Postman Collections

Work with B2B and D2C APIs using pre-built collections.

### B2B and D2C Commerce Release Notes

Learn about new features in B2B and D2C Commerce, Salesforce Order Management, and Salesforce Payments.

## Discover Point of Sale for Developers

Explore content for Point of Sale (POS) implementations. Extend your POS operations with comprehensive APIs, SPIs, and webhooks that enable seamless integration with external systems.

## Point of Sale for Developers

Access developer guides and API reference documentation for Point of Sale.

Sign up to receive the monthly Salesforce Developer Newsletter so you never miss the latest announcements, blogs, videos, or Agentforce NOW events.

# Authentication and Authorization

To make sure that the setup is complete, you must provide a scope for custom code execution and also a scope for API administration:

* Functional scopes (`c_` prefix): These custom scopes authorize the execution of your specific business logic. They handle the request authorization for the code itself.
* Diagnostic/Administrative Scope (`sfcc.custom-apis` and `sfcc.custom-apis.rw`): This scope is required to access the DX API. While your `c_` scope runs your custom code, the `sfcc.custom-apis` scope provides the necessary visibility into the registration status and scaffolding of the Custom API framework.

Custom APIs must be secured by a security scheme which includes exactly one functional scope. Custom API clients must obtain a token with the required scope. To secure your custom endpoints and make authorized requests to them, complete the following steps:

1. Choose a security scheme and custom scope for the endpoint.
2. Update your API client to include the custom scope in tokens.

The Custom APIs DX endpoint uses an Account Manager OAuth 2.0 bearer token for authentication and you must specify one of the following scopes to access this API endpoint:

`sfcc.custom-apis`: Provides read-only access.
`sfcc.custom-apis.rw`: Provides read-write acc

For additional Custom API DX details, see Custom APIs Authentication and Authorization.

Your Custom API endpoints must be associated with a security scheme in the API contract.

* `ShopperToken`: For Shopper APIs and storefront use cases. Use Shopper Login and API Access to obtain tokens.
* `AmOAuth2`: For SCAPI Admin APIs to be used with backoffice apps. Use Account Manager to obtain tokens.

Association is either per operation or global, with the operation scheme taking precedence. The schemes are the same as those used for non-custom B2C Commerce APIs (SCAPI).

The scheme must set exactly one custom scope.

Schemes used in the contract must be defined in the `components` section, for example:

Custom scopes must meet the following requirements:

* The name must begin with `c_`.
* The name must not contain characters other than alphanumeric, period, hyphen and underscore.
* The name must not be more than 25 characters.

Endpoints without correct scheme or scope assignments are not registered.

You can review registration errors by searching in the Log Center for messages with a category that includes `CustomApiRegistry`.



Scopes for `ShopperLogin` can be assigned to a client in the SLAS Admin UI. For example:

To obtain a SLAS token, follow the steps in the Shopper Login overview.

Custom scopes for `AmOAuth2` can be assigned to a client in Account Manager. For example:

To obtain an Account Manager token follow the steps in the Authorization for Admin APIs guide.

Unauthorized requests receive a `401 Unauthorized` response.

# B2C Commerce API (SCAPI) Specifications

You are viewing SCAPI documentation. To view the full SCAPI reference specifications in the left navigation, select the **Reference** tab (if you are currently in the **Guides** tab).

To view additional API specifications:
